rows.en: Arthur: "Oh, Touya.
Is something wrong?"
Yamato: "Oh, he's reading..."
Touya: "Looks like he's concentrating."
Yamato: "We shouldn't disturb him."
Touya: "But we've got a proper reason to see him..."
Yamato: "Well, yes, but..."
Arthur: "...? Oh, Touya."
Touya: "Oh, do you have a moment?"
Arthur: "Yes, of course."
Touya: "About what happened in the galley the other day..."
Arthur: "The galley...? Oh, Ymir...
Do you mean when I helped her?"
Touya: "Yeah. I didn't expect you to be that good
at cooking."
Arthur: "My mother was often ill in bed.
I picked it up naturally while looking after my younger siblings."
Yamato: "Oh? Do you have a lot of siblings, Arthur?"
Arthur: "Two younger brothers and one younger sister.
It's been three years... My sister should be sixteen, and my youngest brother ten
by now."
Touya: "How old are you again, Arthur?"
Arthur: "Twenty-five."
Yamato: "There's quite a gap, meow."
Arthur: "Yes..."
Touya: "? What's wrong?"
Arthur: "No, it's nothing.
We were talking about cooking, weren't we?"
Touya: "Y-Yeah..."
Arthur: "Besides at home, I cooked in the cafeteria
of the factory where I worked.
I was quite popular, you know."
Yamato: "I see, meow... That's why you were so efficient.
It was so rhythmic, I couldn't help admiring it."
Arthur: "Heh heh... Thank you."
Touya: "Come to think of it, you were talking about silk before..."
Arthur: "Oh, would you like to hear about it again?"
Touya: "N-No, I'll pass.
That's not what I mean. If you've got an acquaintance like that,
aren't you fairly well off?"
Yamato: "But Arthur's always so neatly dressed,
and somehow he seems like he grew up in a well-off family,
doesn't he? Unlike Touya."
Yamato: "Owww!"
Touya: "You could've left off that last bit.
...But yeah, he does seem well brought up."
Arthur: "It's true that my home is in Zimbabwe's capital,
but we aren't particularly wealthy.
My father even cut back on his own food expenses
so I could get an education.
Without him, I wouldn't be who I am now...
He's a wonderful man everyone likes, my father."
Yamato: "You respect him."
Arthur: "Yes. My mother was able to pass away happy
thanks to my father..."
Yamato: "What? But you said she was often ill in bed..."
Arthur: "Oh, yes... Um, my father remarried.
My birth mother died of illness when I was five."
Yamato: "Oh... I-I'm sorry, meow..."
Arthur: "Don't worry about it.
My mother passed away surrounded by my father's love, and she still lives
in my heart..."
Touya: "I see... So you were poor?"
Yamato: "Touya!"
Arthur: "Ha ha ha. Yes.
We may have been... poor.
But I never once felt that way."
Touya: "?"
Arthur: "...Suppose a train is running.
It has carriages divided into first through fourth class.
Riding first class costs dozens of times what fourth class
does. But the train is heading straight
for its destination.
Being in first class doesn't make you arrive any sooner,
and being uncomfortable doesn't mean you won't reach
the destination.
All the people on that train are headed in the same, right direction
as they travel."
Touya: "???"
Arthur: "Well, I should be going now.
Until next time."
Touya: "...What did that mean?"
Yamato: "He means it's all in how you look at things, doesn't he, meow?"
Touya: "Hmm..."
Yamato: "Anyway, let's go, too."
